findings.title: webauthnAuth null check inconsistent with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled usage
findings.body: action() calls `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()` directly, but authenticate()/challenge() now use `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which additionally requires `user != null`. During normal login (no user set yet) with passkeys enabled, action() will still try to route webauthn form submissions via webauthnAuth, but authenticate()/challenge() will no longer call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when user==null, since previously the old code called fillContextForm when user was null (conditional UI case). This reverses the previous conditional-UI behavior: conditional UI (discoverable login with no selected user) must have fillContextForm invoked when user is null, but the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled explicitly requires user != null, which will break conditional UI passkey flows where no user is pre-selected.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled called without context/user
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the inherited method signature in UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. This implies either a missing no-arg overload exists elsewhere undocumented, or this code does not compile. If there is a separate no-arg overload, its semantics (ignoring the user) differ from the single-arg version used elsewhere, causing inconsistent behavior between UsernameForm and UsernamePasswordForm when deciding to skip the form for an already-authenticated user ignoring whether they actually have passkeys registered.

findings.title: Reauthentication form flags not reset on success path first render
findings.body: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes when an error occurs, duplicating logic previously in authenticate(). Because this is now spread across three call sites (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, UsernamePasswordForm, WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator) there's a risk that one path (e.g. WebAuthnAuthenticator.setErrorResponse for 2FA errors) never calls this helper, so hidden-username state could be lost/inconsistent on certain error branches, leading to the username field reappearing unexpectedly during re-authentication errors routed through WebAuthnAuthenticator rather than WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.
